findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a detached logger, so calls through it are not recorded
findings.body: `FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()`, a fresh logger. `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` (logger_middleware.go:58). If a test wires a `*log.TestLogger` into `NewLoggerMiddleware`, the `Info` call lands on the throwaway logger and `logger.InfoLogs` stays at zero calls. Assertions of the form `Calls == 0` pass silently, and `Calls == 1` fails with no hint why. Returning `f` (the same logger) would keep the recorded logs visible through the fake. No test in the repo does this today (grep: no clientmiddleware logger test uses NewTestLogger), so this is about the next test that does.
findings.originReason: This diff adds the `FromContext` fake, which returns a new logger.

verification.reason: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()`, a new logger. `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now logs through `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, so a `TestLogger` passed into the middleware would never record that Info call.

findings.title: No test covers the log fields that moved from LoggerMiddleware to the context
findings.body: The `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `uname`, `dsName`, `dsUID` and `traceID` fields used to be added explicitly in `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` (logger_middleware.go:36-60 before this PR). They now reach the log line only through the context: `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` (this file) -> `log.WithContextualAttributes` -> the infra `ctxLogProviders` (pkg/infra/log/log.go:55-61) and the tracing provider (pkg/infra/tracing/tracing.go:91-97). The only test touched here is metrics_middleware_test.go, and it asserts metrics only, not log output. There is no logger_middleware_test.go and no test for `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware`. A test that runs a request through the chain and checks the emitted fields would pin this contract, which now spans three packages.
findings.originReason: This PR moves the fields from explicit log params to context attributes and adds no test for the new path.

verification.reason: In the base, `logRequest` added pluginId, endpoint, uname, traceID, dsName and dsUID itself. In the head these fields only reach the log line through the context attributes. The clientmiddleware package has no test file for either the logger or the contextual logger middleware.

findings.title: Test still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware after the type was renamed to MetricsMiddleware
findings.body: The PR renames `InstrumentationMiddleware` to `MetricsMiddleware` and `newInstrumentationMiddleware` to `newMetricsMiddleware`, and this test now calls `newMetricsMiddleware` (line 78). The test function name at line 21 still says `Instrumentation`, which points readers at a type that no longer exists. Renaming it to `TestMetricsMiddleware` would match the code under test.
findings.originReason: The name matched the type in the base. The rename in this PR is what makes it stale.

verification.reason: The test function is still named `TestInstrumentationMiddleware`, but the type is now `MetricsMiddleware` and the test calls `newMetricsMiddleware`.

findings.title: instrumentContext is a misleading name for a function that only attaches logger attributes
findings.body: The helper was moved here from the metrics middleware, where the name fit less badly. Here it only builds the contextual log attributes and calls `log.WithContextualAttributes`, and it is no longer part of instrumentation. The name and its doc comment (line 26) suggest it does metrics work. Something like `withPluginLogAttributes` would describe what it does.

verification.reason: `instrumentContext` was moved unchanged from the instrumentation middleware into the contextual logger middleware. Its only job is to attach log attributes, so the 'instrument' name is a misleading leftover in its new home.

findings.title: FromContext doc comment is copied from New and does not say where the attributes come from
findings.body: The comment on `FromContext` (line 22) repeats the wording of `New` (line 7): 'returns a new contextual Logger that has this logger's context plus the given context'. For `FromContext`, the extra attributes come from the context value (through the contextual log providers in pkg/infra/log/log.go:203-217), not from an argument. Readers cannot tell the two methods apart from the comments. The comment should say that the attributes are read from ctx, and that the logger is returned unchanged when ctx carries none.

verification.reason: The new `FromContext` doc comment repeats `New`'s wording word for word. It never says that the attributes are read from ctx through the context log providers.

findings.title: Context attributes may be appended into a parent's slice that shares its backing array
findings.body: `instrumentContext` calls `log.WithContextualAttributes(ctx, p)` (line 36). In pkg/infra/log/log.go:285-291 that function does `append(ctx.Value(logParamsContextKey{}).([]any), logParams...)` when the parent context already carries attributes. If the parent slice has spare capacity, the append writes into the parent's backing array. Two child contexts derived from the same parent and running concurrently can then overwrite each other's `dsName`/`uname` values, and the logs of one request can show another's values. The same call sat in instrumentPluginRequest before this PR, so this does not regress here. It is a latent problem for any nested call that reuses a context already carrying attributes. I did not confirm that such nested calls happen in practice. The fix belongs in the infra helper (copy before append), not in this file.
findings.originReason: The base made the same `WithContextualAttributes` call from `instrumentPluginRequest`, and the infra helper is unchanged.

verification.reason: `WithContextualAttributes` appends directly onto the parent's slice. The stored slice can have spare capacity (four elements appended up to six gives cap 8), so sibling contexts could share a backing array. The only production caller is this middleware, and no nested call path was found, so this is a latent issue only.

contracts.action: ContextualLoggerMiddleware attaches endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID and uname to the request context for QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth and CollectMetrics
contracts.equivalent_path: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware.go:104-113 (before this PR, instrumentPluginRequest called instrumentContext before fn; that call is removed in the head)
contracts.before_after: Before: enrichment ran inside MetricsMiddleware.instrumentPluginRequest after the plugin-registry lookup succeeded, and only for the four endpoints. After: enrichment runs in its own middleware placed after MetricsMiddleware and before LoggerMiddleware, for the same four endpoints. Downstream middlewares still receive the enriched context. MetricsMiddleware no longer enriches the context, but nothing between Metrics and the new middleware reads the attributes.
contracts.visible_effect: Same keys on the same log line for the logged endpoints. Only the order of the keys in the logfmt line changes.
contracts.failure_mode: A nil req panics at contextual_logger_middleware.go:40 and in the other three methods. This is not new: MetricsMiddleware dereferences req.PluginContext and req.Queries before this middleware runs (metrics_middleware.go:144-149, 169-171). A non-nil req cannot fail here.

contracts.action: LoggerMiddleware.logRequest emits 'Plugin Request Completed' through m.logger.FromContext(ctx) instead of setting pluginId, endpoint, uname, traceID, dsName and dsUID on the log call
contracts.equivalent_path: pkg/infra/log/log.go:203-217 (ConcreteLogger.FromContext, which applies the registered providers); pkg/infra/log/log.go:55-61 (provider for WithContextualAttributes); pkg/infra/tracing/tracing.go:91-97 (provider that emits traceID)
contracts.before_after: Before: the fields were added to logParams in logRequest, and traceID came from tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false). After: the fields come from the context through the providers, and traceID comes from the tracing provider. The field set matches. The order of keys changes.
contracts.visible_effect: The same field names appear on the 'Plugin Request Completed' line. traceID still appears when tracing has set one.
contracts.failure_mode: If the context carries no attributes, the line loses pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID and uname without any error. In CreateMiddlewares, ContextualLoggerMiddleware is always placed before LoggerMiddleware (pluginsintegration.go:160-161), so this does not happen in the product. LoggerMiddleware is only built in CreateMiddlewares (grep).

contracts.action: grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext converts the infra logger for a context into a plugin logger
contracts.equivalent_path: pkg/infra/log/log.go:203-217 (ConcreteLogger.FromContext always returns *ConcreteLogger, through cl or cl.New)
contracts.before_after: There was no equivalent before. The new method keeps the logger's name because cl.New wraps the same SwapLogger chain, so the 'logger' key set by log.New is preserved.
contracts.visible_effect: Log lines from LoggerMiddleware keep logger=plugin.instrumentation with the contextual fields added.
contracts.failure_mode: The type assertion at logger.go:49 cannot fail, since ConcreteLogger.FromContext always returns *ConcreteLogger. The fallback at logger.go:51 is dead code. Nothing is lost silently.

contracts.equivalent_path: pkg/plugins/log/fake.go:18-20 (TestLogger.New, which also returns a fresh NewTestLogger())
contracts.before_after: There was no FromContext before. The new method returns a detached logger, so the calls it receives are not recorded on the original TestLogger.
contracts.visible_effect: No product effect. Tests that assert on the original logger's InfoLogs after code calls FromContext will see no calls.
contracts.failure_mode: Assertions on the original fake's logs silently miss calls routed through FromContext (see the finding at fake.go:46).

contracts.action: Logger interface gains FromContext; the middleware chain changes from InstrumentationMiddleware to MetricsMiddleware plus ContextualLoggerMiddleware
contracts.equivalent_path: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/pluginsintegration.go:158 (TracingMiddleware is the sibling constructor in the same list)
contracts.before_after: Before: one InstrumentationMiddleware did metrics and enrichment. After: MetricsMiddleware, then ContextualLoggerMiddleware, then LoggerMiddleware. The metric names, labels and the logger name 'plugin.instrumentation' are unchanged (pluginsintegration.go:161).
contracts.visible_effect: Metric names and labels are unchanged, and the logger name in the logs is unchanged.
contracts.failure_mode: Every implementer of the interface must now provide FromContext. A grep for implementers finds only grafanaInfraLogWrapper (logger.go) and TestLogger (fake.go), and both implement it. Nothing else in the repo references NewInstrumentationMiddleware. Nothing is lost silently.

summary: Behaviour is preserved on the product path: the same fields reach the same log line, metric names and labels are unchanged, and the traceID that the PR drops is still emitted through the tracing context provider. I found no blocker or fix. Four consider-level findings: TestLogger.FromContext returns a detached logger (fake.go:46), no test covers the moved log fields (contextual_logger_middleware.go:14), a stale test name (metrics_middleware_test.go:21), and a misleading helper name and a copied doc comment. There is also a latent slice-aliasing risk in the infra helper that the call site inherits (contextual_logger_middleware.go:36, pre-existing, not changed by this PR). I read pluginsintegration.go lines 130-190 rather than the whole file; the only change in it is at 157-161. The repository has no docs/adr directory in this snapshot, so there was no ADR to check against.
